title: Teams: chat, channel, component-only, scope refresh; no kinship from equal thread IDs
annotator: claude-sonnet-5.5 worker, hand annotation on 2026-10-24 (hand-reading by a language model; no human review; no program produced any expected value)
independence_statement: Scopes, IDs and reply links are invented by hand. Expected grouping outcomes follow the written rules in preparation-semantics.md and the Teams release rows of the handoff spec. No grouping or A2 code was run or imported.

sources: ADDED CASES P06 to P08, N07 to N09 (independent follow-up for review finding M2): hand-written by a language model (Claude Sonnet 5.5 worker) from preparation-semantics.md (parent edges, scope-incompatible ancestry) and the A1 Teams plan docs/plans/2026-10-03-teams-a1-readonly-acquisition-plan (observed message versions, deletion only with provider evidence). No program produced any value. T0-03-N07 is PROPOSED: no A1 text says how A2 treats a record without an id. It needs owner sign-off.
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-03-a1-a2-handoff-contract-design.md: Teams extension table (chat discover, channel discover, notification reconcile)
tests/teams_support.py and tests/teams_ordering_support.py (A1 Teams fixture shapes, read only)

cases.title: Channel root and reply in one scope form a confirmed group
Chat messages stay separate without an explicit reply link

expected.reason: chat membership and time proximity are not grouping rules

cases.title: Chat reply with explicit resolvable teams_chat_reply_to confirms
Component-only observation does not create a message record
cases.rationale: Spec: Teams chat discovery has positive observations, topology and independent component effects. A component effect is not a message.

cases.title: Scope refresh keeps old versions under the old scope reference

expected.reason: native confirmation needs exactly the same scope reference; a changed scope reference is explicit uncertainty

cases.title: Reply to a reply in one channel scope: all three records form one confirmed group
cases.rationale: preparation-semantics.md: confirmed groups are connected components of unambiguous exact parent edges. The chain has two edges for three members.

cases.title: Edited channel message: both observed versions stay as separate records
cases.rationale: A1 plan (docs/plans/2026-10-03-teams-a1-readonly-acquisition-plan): persist every observed message version keyed by scoped identity and provider version or etag. The case fixes only that the versions stay distinct. It does not fix a group status, because the A1 text is silent on grouping between versions of one message.

cases.title: Message with a provider deletedDateTime is marked deleted
cases.rationale: A1 plan (docs/plans/2026-10-03-teams-a1-readonly-acquisition-plan): mark message deletion only when the provider exposes deletedDateTime, a proven delta tombstone, or a persisted change notification.

cases.title: Equal thread ID in two different channel scopes is not kinship
Equal thread ID between a chat and a channel is not kinship
Reply whose parent lives in another scope is not joined

expected.reason: parent has a different declared scope

cases.title: Chat members with the same display name are not one person-thread
Missing channel root is uncertain, not invented
Truncated record without its required id is not accepted and no id is invented
cases.rationale: PROPOSED. A1 Teams discovery code requires a non-empty source id (message_ingest/spiders/microsoft/teams/_base.py), but no A1 text says what A2 does with a record that arrives without one. The value is the plain safe answer: no guess, and a visible failure.

cases.title: Chat reply whose parent is in another chat scope is not joined

expected.reason: parent has a different declared scope

cases.rationale: preparation-semantics.md: 'A parent with a different source kind or declared source scope is not joined' and scope-incompatible ancestry is an explicit uncertain disposition. T0-03-N03 covers the channel kind. This case covers the chat kind.

cases.title: Absence from a later list is not a deletion

expected.reason: absence can come from loss of access, retention or API visibility

cases.rationale: A1 plan (docs/plans/2026-10-03-teams-a1-readonly-acquisition-plan): do not mark a chat, channel, member or message deleted merely because it is absent from a later list.
